mic_help.title: Microphone troubleshooting
mic_help.intro: If the app can't hear your guitar or detects the wrong notes, work through these steps. Most issues come from browser permissions or another app using the mic.
mic_help.reset_hint: Clears this app's saved calibration and mic preferences, then reloads the page.

0.title: Allow microphone access
0.description: Click the lock / mic icon in your browser's address bar and make sure this site is allowed to use the microphone. If you accidentally blocked it, switch it back to "Allow" and reload the page.

1.title: Pick the right input device
1.description: If you have several mics or an audio interface, set the correct one as the default input in your system sound settings (and in the browser's site permissions), then reload.

2.title: Free up the microphone
2.description: Close other apps that might be holding the mic — Zoom, Discord, OBS, Teams, or another browser tab. Only one app can capture a low-latency input at a time.

3.title: Recalibrate
3.description: Use the Recalibrate button to re-run the tuning calibration. This fixes most "notes not detected" or "wrong note" problems after changing gear or rooms.

4.title: Check levels & tuning
4.description: Make sure your guitar is in tune and loud enough. Move closer to the mic, raise the input gain, and reduce background noise. Very quiet or distorted signals are hard to detect.

5.title: Check OS privacy settings
5.description: On Windows: Settings → Privacy & security → Microphone, and allow your browser. On macOS: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone. The browser must be enabled there too.

6.title: Clear cookies & site data
6.description: Stale permissions or cached data can break capture. Clear cookies and site data for this site in your browser settings, then reload and allow the mic again. (Use the reset button below to clear this app's saved mic setup.)

7.title: Try another browser
7.description: Chrome and Edge have the most reliable audio capture. Some browsers throttle or block the mic in background tabs or on insecure connections — keep this tab focused and on https.

timing.title: Calibrate timing
timing.intro: Speakers, headphones and audio interfaces each add a delay between the click you hear and the note we pick up. Play along to a few clicks and we'll measure yours, so timing grades match what you hear.
timing.step1: Use the speakers or headphones you practice with.
timing.step2: Pluck the open low E on every click and let it ring — don't mute between clicks. {{bpm}} BPM, {{countIn}} clicks to get ready, then {{clicks}} counted.
timing.step3: Play with the click, not ahead of it.
timing.forget: Forget the measurement and go back to the estimate
timing.get_ready: Get ready — listen to the pulse

fail.ahead: The notes came in ahead of the click
fail.spread: The hits were too spread out
fail.too_few_body: We picked up {{hits}} of {{total}} — it takes at least {{min}}. Pluck a little harder, and check the mic is the one your guitar is on.
fail.ahead_body: Sound can't reach us before it's played, so something else was heard. Let the string ring between clicks instead of muting it, and play with the click, not ahead of it.
fail.spread_body: They wandered by about ±{{spread}} ms, which says more about the run than about your setup. Try again, playing right on the click and letting the string ring.

timing.heard: {{hits}} of {{total}} clicks heard, steady within ±{{spread}} ms
